## Critique
- claim-1: Correctly grounded. The original variable module includes every \(A_{\lambda,\theta}\) with \(\theta\subseteq(n-r)^r\), not merely \(\theta\subseteq(n-r-i)^j\).
- claim-2: Correctly grounded. The cited specialization argument is invalid: specializing an inconsistent system need not preserve inconsistency.
- claim-3: Correct. The listed Littlewood–Richardson coefficients follow from Pieri, and the example explicitly shows that \(A_{\varnothing,(2)}\) cannot be discarded.
- claim-4: Correct, but it refutes only the proposed projected-row repair; it does not rule out another extension or a direct inconsistency proof.
- claim-5: Accurate for the specialist output. The missing certificate is nevertheless supplied below by an integral Hopf-algebra identity requiring no enlargement.

## Repair certificates
- [proof-attempt] Put \(q=n-r\) and define the full original variable module
  \[
  X_\varphi=
  \bigoplus_{\substack{\lambda\subseteq b^a,\ |\lambda|<N\\
  \theta\subseteq q^r,\ |\theta|=N-|\lambda|}}
  \mathbb Z A_{\lambda,\theta}.
  \]
  No coordinate is discarded. In particular, whenever admissible, \(A_{\varnothing,(2)}\in X_\varphi\).

  Let \(\overline\Lambda=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\) and
  \[
  T(A_{\lambda,\theta})=\bar s_\lambda\otimes\bar s_\theta .
  \]
  Since the indicated Schur classes are basis elements of \(\overline\Lambda\), \(T\) is injective on \(X_\varphi\). For a decomposable row with bottom and right components \(B,R\), the established row–tensor correspondence is
  \[
  T(\operatorname{Lin}_\varphi(\nu))
  =\mathrm{CP}(\bar s_B\otimes\bar s_R)
  \]
  [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 428-493].

  Let \(\rho\) be tall and write \(\beta=\rho_B\). Then
  \[
  \beta\subseteq b^a,\qquad |\beta|=N,\qquad \rho_R=\varnothing,
  \]
  and hence
  \[
  T(\operatorname{Lin}_\varphi(\rho))
  =\mathrm{CP}(\bar s_\beta\otimes1).
  \]
  In \(\Lambda\otimes\Lambda\), the following integral identity holds:
  \[
  \boxed{\;
  \mathrm{CP}(s_\beta\otimes1)=
  \sum_{\substack{\lambda,\mu\\ \mu\ne\varnothing}}
  (-1)^{|\mu|+1}c_{\lambda,\mu}^{\beta}\,
  \mathrm{CP}(s_\lambda\otimes s_{\mu'})
  \;}
  \tag{*}
  \]
  where \(\mathrm{CP}(s_\beta\otimes1)=\Delta(s_\beta)-s_\beta\otimes1\), while
  \(\mathrm{CP}(s_\lambda\otimes s_{\mu'})
  =\Delta(s_\lambda)(1\otimes s_{\mu'})\).

  To prove \((*)\), use \(S(s_\mu)=(-1)^{|\mu|}s_{\mu'}\) and coassociativity:
  \[
  \begin{aligned}
  \sum_{\lambda,\mu}c_{\lambda,\mu}^{\beta}
  \Delta(s_\lambda)(1\otimes S(s_\mu))
  &=\sum s_{\beta(1)}\otimes
       s_{\beta(2)}S(s_{\beta(3)})\\
  &=s_\beta\otimes1.
  \end{aligned}
  \]
  The unique term with \(\mu=\varnothing\) is
  \(\Delta(s_\beta)\). Moving it to the other side and substituting the
  antipode formula gives \((*)\). All coefficients are integers
  [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 702-735].

  Every term on the right of \((*)\) is an original wide row. Indeed,
  \(c_{\lambda,\mu}^{\beta}\ne0\) implies
  \[
  \lambda,\mu\subseteq\beta,\qquad |\lambda|<N.
  \]
  Set \(R=\mu'\). Then
  \[
  R\subseteq\beta'\subseteq a^b\subseteq(q-i)^j,
  \]
  using \(a+i\le q\) and \(b\le j\). Pad \(R\) to \(j\) parts and \(\lambda\) to \(a\) parts, and define
  \[
  \nu_{\lambda,\mu}
   =(i+R_1,\ldots,i+R_j,\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_a).
  \]
  This is a partition because \(\lambda_1\le b\le i\). Moreover,
  \[
  \nu_{\lambda,\mu}\subseteq q^r,\qquad
  |\nu_{\lambda,\mu}|=ij+N,\qquad
  (\nu_{\lambda,\mu})_{j+1}\le b,\qquad
  \ell(\nu_{\lambda,\mu})\le j+a\le r.
  \]
  Since \(R\ne\varnothing\), it is wide. Its components are exactly
  \(B=\lambda\) and \(R=\mu'\). Projecting \((*)\) to
  \(\overline\Lambda\otimes\overline\Lambda\) and using injectivity of \(T\) therefore yields the full-coordinate integral identity
  \[
  \operatorname{Lin}_\varphi(\rho)=
  \sum_{\substack{\lambda,\mu\\\mu\ne\varnothing}}
  (-1)^{|\mu|+1}c_{\lambda,\mu}^{\beta}\,
  \operatorname{Lin}_\varphi(\nu_{\lambda,\mu}).
  \tag{**}
  \]

  Thus, in any putative solution with every wide right-hand side zero, \((**)\) forces every tall right-hand side to be zero. This contradicts the hypothesis that some tall right-hand side is nonzero. Hence the original system is inconsistent, including the large-\(N\) range, without enlargement.

  For the counterexample parameters and \(\beta=(2)\), \((**)\) reads
  \[
  \operatorname{Lin}(2,2,2)
  =\operatorname{Lin}(3,2,1)-\operatorname{Lin}(3,3),
  \]
  namely
  \[
  (1,0,1)=(1,1,1)-(0,1,0)
  \]
  in the full column order
  \[
  \bigl(A_{\varnothing,(2)},A_{\varnothing,(1,1)},A_{(1),(1)}\bigr).
  \]

## Required revisions
- Replace the false enlargement/projection step with the integral identity \((**)\).
- Retain all original coordinates; no restriction \(\theta\subseteq(q-i)^j\) is imposed on \(X_\varphi\).
- The scoped large-\(N\) inconsistency certificate is established by this direct argument. No parent-theorem conclusion is asserted.
